label: Background by volume
value: Born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia, to schoolteachers Walter and Bertha Shirley, who both died of fever when she was three months old

label: Background by volume
value: Raised in poverty by Mrs. Thomas and later Mrs. Hammond, helping to care for numerous children and twins

label: Background by volume
value: Lived in the Hopeton Orphanage for four months before being brought to Prince Edward Island

label: Background by volume
value: Adopted by sibling farmers Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert of Green Gables in Avonlea

label: Background by volume
value: Attended Queen's Academy, earning a First Class Teacher's License and winning the Avery Scholarship

label: Background by volume
value: Gave up her college scholarship to stay at Green Gables and teach in Avonlea after Matthew Cuthbert's death

label: Background by volume
value: Attended Redmond College in Kingsport, graduating with a Bachelor of Arts degree and winning the Thorburn Scholarship

label: Background by volume
value: Served as Principal of Summerside High School for three years prior to her marriage

label: Appearance
value: Anne is tall
unit: Anne is tall, slender, and graceful, with an oval face, a milk-white skin, and large, expressive gray-green eyes that shine with starry brightness. She has a clear, delicate, pointed chin, a shapely nose, and a mobile face that vividly reflects her inner emotions. Her thick hair, famously red and freckled in her childhood, darkens as she matures into a rich, glossy auburn.

value: Anne is intensely imaginative.
unit: Anne is an intensely imaginative, passionate, and romantic individual who possesses a deep love for nature and beauty. Though quick-tempered and prone to dramatic daydreams in her youth, she matures into a wise, empathetic, and sweet-tempered woman while retaining her youthful zest for life and capacity for joy. She has a natural gift for winning the affection of others, particularly children and kindred spirits, and possesses a subtle, irrepressible sense of humor.

label: History
value: Anne Shirley arrived at Green Gables in Avonlea by mistake.
unit: Anne Shirley arrived at Green Gables in Avonlea by mistake, as Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert had intended to adopt a boy to help on their farm; however, they quickly decided to keep her. She formed an enduring bosom-friendship with her neighbor Diana Barry and developed a fierce school rivalry with Gilbert Blythe after he called her 'Carrots.' Over her girlhood years in Avonlea, Anne got into various humorous and dramatic scrapes, including accidentally intoxicating Diana with currant wine and dying her hair green, but earned the affection of the community through her sweetness, bright mind, and vivid imagination. After attending Queen's Academy and winning the Avery Scholarship, Anne chose to remain at Green Gables to teach in Avonlea and care for Marilla following Matthew's sudden death. During her time as a schoolteacher, she organized the Avonlea Village Improvement Society and befriended many neighbors, including the eccentric Mr. Harrison, Paul Irving, and Miss Lavendar Lewis. She later attended Redmond College in Kingsport alongside her friends, earning her B.A. degree and rejecting a marriage proposal from the wealthy Roy Gardner when she realized she did not truly love him. Reconciling with Gilbert Blythe after he recovered from a dangerous bout of typhoid fever, Anne realized her love for him and accepted his proposal. Following three years of teaching in Summerside, Anne married Gilbert in the orchard at Green Gables. The newlyweds settled at Four Winds Harbor in a cozy cottage dubbed the 'house of dreams,' where Anne befriended her tragic neighbor Leslie Moore and the lighthouse keeper Captain Jim. After tragically losing her firstborn infant daughter, Joyce, Anne gave birth to a healthy son, James Matthew ('Jem'). When Gilbert's medical practice expanded, the family relocated to the larger estate of Ingleside in Glen St. Mary, where Anne raised her growing family—Jem, Walter, twins Nan and Di, Shirley, and Rilla—and welcomed her old friend Mrs.

unit: Anne Shirley arrived at Green Gables in Avonlea by mistake, as Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert had intended to adopt a boy to help on their farm; however, they quickly decided to keep her. She formed an enduring bosom-friendship with her neighbor Diana Barry and developed a fierce school rivalry with Gilbert Blythe after he called her 'Carrots.' Over her girlhood years in Avonlea, Anne got into various humorous and dramatic scrapes, including accidentally intoxicating Diana with currant wine and dying her hair green, but earned the affection of the community through her sweetness, bright mind, and vivid imagination. After attending Queen's Academy and winning the Avery Scholarship, Anne chose to remain at Green Gables to teach in Avonlea and care for Marilla following Matthew's sudden death. During her time as a schoolteacher, she organized the Avonlea Village Improvement Society and befriended many neighbors, including the eccentric Mr. Harrison, Paul Irving, and Miss Lavendar Lewis. She later attended Redmond College in Kingsport alongside her friends, earning her B.A. degree and rejecting a marriage proposal from the wealthy Roy Gardner when she realized she did not truly love him. Reconciling with Gilbert Blythe after he recovered from a dangerous bout of typhoid fever, Anne realized her love for him and accepted his proposal. Following three years of teaching in Summerside, Anne married Gilbert in the orchard at Green Gables. The newlyweds settled at Four Winds Harbor in a cozy cottage dubbed the 'house of dreams,' where Anne befriended her tragic neighbor Leslie Moore and the lighthouse keeper Captain Jim. After tragically losing her firstborn infant daughter, Joyce, Anne gave birth to a healthy son, James Matthew ('Jem'). When Gilbert's medical practice expanded, the family relocated to the larger estate of Ingleside in Glen St. Mary, where Anne raised her growing family—Jem, Walter, twins Nan and Di, Shirley, and Rilla—and welcomed her old friend Mrs.

label: History
value: Anthony Pye was taken in by Mr. George Pye.
unit: Anthony Pye was taken in by his uncle and aunt, Mr. and Mrs. George Pye of Avonlea, as an orphan nephew. When Anne Shirley took over the Avonlea school, Anthony was one of her new pupils and immediately displayed a hostile and rebellious attitude, declaring that female teachers were 'no good.' He engaged in persistent minor misconduct, such as pouring water down a classmate's neck and placing a live mouse in Anne's desk to mock her. When confronted, he insolently admitted to the prank, prompting Anne to lose her temper and whip him with a pointer. Following this punishment, Anthony's attitude shifted remarkably; he began showing respect toward Anne, offering to carry her books and acknowledging her capability as a teacher. In later school years, he violently defended Anne's reputation when other boys spoke ill of her.

When Anne Shirley took over the Avonlea school, Anthony was one of her new pupils and immediately displayed a hostile and rebellious attitude, declaring that female teachers were 'no good.' He engaged in persistent minor misconduct, such as pouring water down a classmate's neck and placing a live mouse in Anne's desk to mock her. When confronted, he insolently admitted to the prank, prompting Anne to lose her temper and whip him with a pointer. Following this punishment, Anthony's attitude shifted remarkably; he began showing respect toward Anne, offering to carry her books and acknowledging her capability as a teacher. In later school years, he violently defended Anne's reputation when other boys spoke ill of her.

label: History
value: Aunt Jamesina was named after her father.
unit: Aunt Jamesina was named after her father, who died at sea before she was born. After her own daughter married and departed for missionary work in India, Aunt Jamesina was left alone in a large house until Stella Maynard invited her to act as matron and housekeeper for a group of Redmond College students. She moved into Patty's Place in Kingsport alongside Anne Shirley, Priscilla Grant, Stella Maynard, and Philippa Gordon, bringing along her cats, Joseph and the Sarah-cat. Over the next two college years, she provided a warm, motherly atmosphere, managing the household, indulging the girls, and adopting a stray cat named Rusty into the family fold. During the holiday seasons she remained behind to look after Patty's Place and the pets. Later, when Anne's firstborn child died, Aunt Jamesina's continued presence and love remained a comfort to the girls as they completed their studies and graduated.

She moved into Patty's Place in Kingsport alongside Anne Shirley, Priscilla Grant, Stella Maynard, and Philippa Gordon, bringing along her cats, Joseph and the Sarah-cat. Over the next two college years, she provided a warm, motherly atmosphere, managing the household, indulging the girls, and adopting a stray cat named Rusty into the family fold. During the holiday seasons she remained behind to look after Patty's Place and the pets. Later, when Anne's firstborn child died, Aunt Jamesina's continued presence and love remained a comfort to the girls as they completed their studies and graduated.

label: History
value: Billy Andrews grew up in Avonlea
unit: Billy Andrews grew up in Avonlea as part of the Andrews family. In his youth, he drove a double-seated buggy to take Anne Shirley, Diana Barry, and his sister Jane to a concert at the White Sands Hotel, secretly admiring Anne. Later, after being given the upper farm by his father, he wished to marry Anne Shirley but was too timid to propose directly, instead persuading his sister Jane to propose on his behalf. After Anne declined his proposal, Billy moved on and married Nettie Blewett, settling down with her on his farm.

label: History
value: Captain Jim grew up in Four Winds, Prince Edward Island.
unit: Captain Jim grew up in Four Winds, Prince Edward Island, and ran away to sea as a boy. In his youth, he fell in love with 'lost Margaret,' who tragically perished at sea during a squall, a loss he mourned for the rest of his life. After decades of adventuring around the globe, he returned to Four Winds and became the keeper of the lighthouse at Four Winds Point. He befriended Gilbert and Anne Blythe when they moved into the nearby 'house of dreams.' Recognizing Owen Ford as a grandson of his old friend, the schoolmaster John Selwyn, Captain Jim collaborated with him to write a book based on his own journal of sea-faring memories. Shortly after receiving a published copy of his completed 'life-book,' Captain Jim passed away peacefully in his sleep at the lighthouse, his hands resting on the volume.

label: History
value: Carl Meredith moved to the Glen St. Mary manse
unit: Carl Meredith moved to the Glen St. Mary manse with his widowed father, John Knox Meredith, his great-aunt Martha, and his siblings Jerry, Faith, and Una. He soon befriended the Blythe children and spent much of his time exploring Rainbow Valley and studying insects. During a game, Carl dropped an eel into Mrs. Carr's buggy, which caused her horse to bolt and angered the community; though he escaped a whipping from his remorseful father, he felt deeply guilty. Later, after running away from a ghost scare at the old Bailey place, Carl accepted a punishment from his brother Jerry to sit alone on a graveyard tombstone at night; as a result of exposure in a cold rain, he developed double pneumonia and nearly died before recovering. After his recovery, his father remarried, giving Carl and his siblings a loving stepmother in Rosemary West.

During a game, Carl dropped an eel into Mrs. Carr's buggy, which caused her horse to bolt and angered the community; though he escaped a whipping from his remorseful father, he felt deeply guilty. Later, after running away from a ghost scare at the old Bailey place, Carl accepted a punishment from his brother Jerry to sit alone on a graveyard tombstone at night; as a result of exposure in a cold rain, he developed double pneumonia and nearly died before recovering. After his recovery, his father remarried, giving Carl and his siblings a loving stepmother in Rosemary West.

label: History
value: Leonora Bowman was born.
unit: Born as Leonora Bowman, she entered the service of Miss Lavendar Lewis at Echo Lodge at age thirteen. Because three of her older sisters had previously worked there, Miss Lavendar affectionately dubbed her 'Charlotta the Fourth.' When Anne Shirley and Diana Barry accidentally stumbled upon Echo Lodge, Charlotta greeted them and assisted Miss Lavendar in entertaining them. Charlotta came to idolize Anne, attempting to mimic her carriage, gestures, and way of speaking. She managed the household at Echo Lodge with fierce devotion, constantly keeping things orderly and protecting her mistress from loneliness or discomfort. When Stephen Irving returned to court Miss Lavendar, Charlotta eagerly supported their romance and helped prepare for their wedding. Following Miss Lavendar's marriage to Stephen Irving, Charlotta moved with them to Boston to continue her service. While in Boston, she married an American bricklayer named Tom, though she retained her fiercely patriotic devotion to Prince Edward Island.

Following Miss Lavendar's marriage to Stephen Irving, Charlotta moved with them to Boston to continue her service. While in Boston, she married an American bricklayer named Tom, though she retained her fiercely patriotic devotion to Prince Edward Island.

label: History
value: Cornelia Bryant lived as an independent spinster in Four Winds.
unit: Cornelia Bryant lived for many years as an independent, outspoken spinster in Four Winds, known for her sharp opinions on men and Methodists and her deep devotion to those in distress. She took a keen interest in Anne Shirley when Anne married Gilbert Blythe and moved to the House of Dreams, becoming one of Anne's closest friends and frequent visitors. Cornelia actively supported community efforts, such as the Avonlea Village Improvement Society and church bazaars, while constantly looking after the neglected and needy, such as Leslie Moore and Mary Vance. After thirty years of courting, she finally agreed to marry her old suitor, Marshall Elliott, upon his shaving his long beard following a Liberal political victory. They married at her home, with Marshall moving into her house. Cornelia continued her benevolent work, taking in the orphaned Mary Vance to raise her, supporting the family of the new Presbyterian minister, Mr. Meredith, and assisting Anne through her joys and sorrows, including the birth and loss of her first child.

label: History
value: Following the death of Mary Keith in East Grafton, Davy and Dora were taken in by Marilla Cuthbert.
unit: Following the death of his mother, Mary Keith, in East Grafton, Davy and his twin sister, Dora, were taken in by their third cousin, Marilla Cuthbert, and brought to live at Green Gables. Davy quickly established himself as a handful, engaging in endless mischief such as dropping a caterpillar down a girl's neck in church, trapping Dora in a toolhouse, placing a toad in Marilla's bed, and stealing plum jam. Despite his misbehavior, he formed a deep emotional bond with Anne Shirley, who patiently guided his moral development and taught him to tell the truth. Upon reaching school age, he attended the Avonlea school and struck up a close friendship with Milty Boulter. Following the death of his uncle Richard Keith, Davy and Dora were permanently adopted at Green Gables when a trust fund was established for their maintenance. As he grew older, Davy reformed many of his unruly habits, developed an interest in farming, and became an affectionate, helpful presence at Green Gables.

label: History
value: Diana Barry meets Anne Shirley
unit: Diana Barry meets Anne Shirley shortly after the latter arrives in Avonlea, and the two young girls solemnly pledge an oath of eternal friendship over running water in the Barry garden. Diana attends the Avonlea school alongside Anne, sharing a desk, games, and childhood secrets. Their friendship faces a temporary crisis when Diana inadvertently becomes intoxicated on Marilla's homemade currant wine, leading Mrs. Barry to forbid the girls from playing together. However, after Anne successfully treats Diana's little sister Minnie May for a life-threatening case of croup during a winter storm, Mrs. Barry relents and reinstates their companionship. As the girls grow up, Diana participates in local events, including the Avonlea Debating Club concerts, the Story Club, and the Avonlea Village Improvement Society. After Anne leaves to attend Queen's Academy and later Redmond College, Diana remains at Orchard Slope, maintaining an affectionate correspondence with Anne. During this time she becomes courted by Fred Wright, a young Avonlea farmer. The two eventually become engaged, and in the summer following Anne's graduation from Redmond College, Diana marries Fred in an old-fashioned wedding at Orchard Slope with Anne as her bridesmaid. The couple settles at their farm in Avonlea, where Diana gives birth to two children, Fred Jr. and Small Anne Cordelia.

unit: Diana Barry meets Anne Shirley shortly after the latter arrives in Avonlea, and the two young girls solemnly pledge an oath of eternal friendship over running water in the Barry garden. Diana attends the Avonlea school alongside Anne, sharing a desk, games, and childhood secrets. Their friendship faces a temporary crisis when Diana inadvertently becomes intoxicated on Marilla's homemade currant wine, leading Mrs. Barry to forbid the girls from playing together. However, after Anne successfully treats Diana's little sister Minnie May for a life-threatening case of croup during a winter storm, Mrs. Barry relents and reinstates their companionship. As the girls grow up, Diana participates in local events, including the Avonlea Debating Club concerts, the Story Club, and the Avonlea Village Improvement Society. After Anne leaves to attend Queen's Academy and later Redmond College, Diana remains at Orchard Slope, maintaining an affectionate correspondence with Anne. During this time she becomes courted by Fred Wright, a young Avonlea farmer. The two eventually become engaged, and in the summer following Anne's graduation from Redmond College, Diana marries Fred in an old-fashioned wedding at Orchard Slope with Anne as her bridesmaid. The couple settles at their farm in Avonlea, where Diana gives birth to two children, Fred Jr. and Small Anne Cordelia.

label: History
value: Dick Moore grew up at Four Winds.
unit: Dick Moore grew up at Four Winds as the son of Abner Moore. In his youth, he worked in his father's store during the winter and went to sea in the summer. Infatuated with the beautiful Leslie West, he pursued her despite her dislike; when she repeatedly refused him, he coerced her mother into forcing the marriage by threatening to foreclose the mortgage on the West farm. After their marriage, Dick continued his wild ways and quickly grew tired of quiet domestic life. The following spring, he sailed on the vessel Four Sisters to Cuba, where he contracted yellow fever and died shortly after the ship was forced to leave without him. For twelve years, his family and the community of Four Winds mistakenly believed that a brain-injured, amnesiac man brought back by Captain Jim was Dick, until a surgical operation in Montreal restored the man's memory, revealing him to be Dick's double cousin, George Moore.

label: History
value: Dora Keith and Davy were twins.
unit: Dora Keith and her twin brother Davy were orphaned in East Grafton when they were six years old. Their third cousin, Marilla Cuthbert, agreed to take them in at Green Gables upon their mother's death. Unlike her turbulent twin brother, Dora settled into life at Green Gables very smoothly, always behaving with utmost propriety, cleanliness, and obedience. She began attending school in Avonlea, sharing a desk with Lily Sloane and later Mirabel Cotton. After her uncle Richard Keith passed away, leaving a trust fund for her and Davy, her permanent home at Green Gables was secured. As she grew older, she inherited Anne Shirley's old porch gable room at Green Gables. By the time she was seventeen, she began receiving romantic attentions from Ralph Andrews.

label: History
value: Ellen West is the elder daughter in the West family.
unit: Ellen West grew up as the elder daughter in the West family. In her youth, she was courted for two years by Norman Douglas, but the two parted after a sudden quarrel. Following her mother's death, Ellen suffered from deep grief and despondency, during which she exacted a solemn promise from her younger sister, Rosemary, that neither of them would ever marry so they could remain together. For years, Ellen and Rosemary lived quietly in the gray house on the hill, keeping out of local society. When Norman Douglas re-entered her life in her later years, he resumed his courtship. label: History
value: Faith moved to the Glen St. Mary manse
unit: Faith moved with her widowed father and siblings to the Glen St. Mary manse from Maywater. Left largely without maternal supervision under the care of their elderly, deaf relative Aunt Martha, she and her brothers and sister often ran wild and unwittingly generated gossip. After meeting the Blythe children in Rainbow Valley, Faith and her family formed a deep and lasting friendship with them. Following a series of misunderstood escapades—including a mix-up over days of the week that led them to clean house on a Sunday—Faith publicly addressed the Glen St. Mary congregation after a service to explain the mistake and defend her father from blame. Soon after, distressed by rumors that the congregation might force her father out, she personally visited the notorious non-churchgoer Norman Douglas to persuade him to return to church, unexpectedly winning his friendship, financial support, and attendance. Deeply sorrowed when Aunt Martha killed her pet rooster Adam for a visiting minister's dinner, she was comforted by Rosemary West, who gifted her a canary. Faith participated enthusiastically in the children's self-governing 'Good-Conduct Club' to keep her family out of trouble. When her father began courting Rosemary West, Faith warmly supported the match, glad to welcome her as a loving presence into their lives.

label: History
value: Gilbert Blythe grows up in Avonlea
unit: Gilbert Blythe grows up in Avonlea and attends the local school, where he quickly becomes Anne Shirley's rival after teasing her about her red hair on his first day back from Alberta. Although Anne refuses to speak to him for years, Gilbert quietly holds a deep affection for her while excelling academically alongside her. After graduating from Queen's Academy, he generously surrenders his application for the Avonlea school so that Anne can teach there and remain near Marilla, taking the White Sands school instead. Later, he attends Redmond College, where he studies diligently, excels in athletics, and wins the prestigious Cooper Prize. After Anne refuses his initial marriage proposal in their Sophomore year, he maintains a respectful distance while continuing his studies and eventually completing his medical degree. After recovering from a severe bout of typhoid fever, he learns that Anne does not love Roy Gardner and renews his suit in Hester Gray's garden, where she accepts him. Following his graduation, he takes over his great-uncle's medical practice in Four Winds Harbor, marries Anne in the orchard at Green Gables, and settles with her in their 'house of dreams.' There they experience the tragic loss of their firstborn infant daughter, Joyce, before welcoming their healthy son, James Matthew ('Jem'). Later, Gilbert purchases the larger Morgan estate at Glen St. Mary to accommodate his growing family and expanding medical practice.

label: History
value: Mr. J. A. Harrison bought Robert Bell's farm in Avonlea
unit: Mr. J. A. Harrison bought Robert Bell's farm in Avonlea and moved there from New Brunswick, initially passing himself off as a bachelor after separating from his wife, Emily, due to domestic disagreements and his profane parrot, Ginger. He gained a reputation in Avonlea for being a crusty, outspoken crank who kept an untidy house. After Anne Shirley's Jersey cow strayed into his oatfield, he had an angry confrontation with her, but they soon reconciled when Anne inadvertently sold his own cow to a trader and personally confessed her mistake. Touched by her honesty, he became good friends with Anne and supported her Village Improvement Society projects. Eventually, his wife Emily discovered his whereabouts through a newspaper item and joined him in Avonlea, leading to their reconciliation and the restoration of an orderly household. Tragically, Ginger was later killed during a violent thunderstorm that struck Four Winds and Avonlea, leaving Mr. Harrison saddened by the loss of his pet. Over the following years, he settled into Avonlea community life, attending church, contributing to the minister's salary, and maintaining a warm, neighborly friendship with the household at Green Gables.

unit: Mr. J. A. Harrison bought Robert Bell's farm in Avonlea and moved there from New Brunswick, initially passing himself off as a bachelor after separating from his wife, Emily, due to domestic disagreements and his profane parrot, Ginger. He gained a reputation in Avonlea for being a crusty, outspoken crank who kept an untidy house. After Anne Shirley's Jersey cow strayed into his oatfield, he had an angry confrontation with her, but they soon reconciled when Anne inadvertently sold his own cow to a trader and personally confessed her mistake. Touched by her honesty, he became good friends with Anne and supported her Village Improvement Society projects. Eventually, his wife Emily discovered his whereabouts through a newspaper item and joined him in Avonlea, leading to their reconciliation and the restoration of an orderly household. Tragically, Ginger was later killed during a violent thunderstorm that struck Four Winds and Avonlea, leaving Mr. Harrison saddened by the loss of his pet. Over the following years, he settled into Avonlea community life, attending church, contributing to the minister's salary, and maintaining a warm, neighborly friendship with the household at Green Gables.

value: Jane grew up in Avonlea.
unit: Jane grew up in Avonlea as a classmate and close friend of Anne Shirley and Diana Barry. After studying at Queen's Academy, she earned her teacher's license and later attended the domestic science course at Redmond College. She taught school first at Newbridge and later in Western Canada. While living in the West, she became engaged to Edward Inglis, a wealthy Winnipeg businessman, and subsequently married him in a lavish ceremony at her family home in Avonlea before moving to Winnipeg and traveling to Europe.

Gentle, tender-hearted, and incapable of harshness, he loves his children deeply, though his detachment often leaves them to manage themselves. label: History
value: Cecilia died.
unit: After the death of his beloved wife Cecilia, John Meredith was left to raise their four young children alone. Upon accepting a call to the Presbyterian church in Glen St. Mary, he moved his family to the parish manse. Due to his intense absorption in theological studies and his dreamer's disposition, he neglected the practical oversight of his household and offspring, leaving them largely under the inadequate care of his aged, ailing relative, Aunt Martha. Although his powerful sermons won the admiration of his congregation, his children's wild pranks and untidy appearances caused frequent local gossip. When Mrs. Alec Davis rudely offered to adopt his daughter Una, Mr. Meredith was severely shaken into recognizing his shortcomings as a father. Determined to make amends and provide a proper mother for his children, he eventually realized his deep affection for Rosemary West. Despite a temporary setback due to an old vow made by Rosemary to her sister, the obstacles were cleared away—largely through the intervention of Una—and Mr. Meredith married Rosemary in a double wedding alongside Norman Douglas and Ellen West.

Following the deaths of her parents, Lavendar remained at Echo Lodge for decades, living a quiet, dream-filled life in near isolation, assisted by a series of young girls whom she called Charlotta. When Anne Shirley and Diana Barry accidentally stumbled upon her home, Lavendar welcomed them warmly, finding in Anne a true kindred spirit. Through Anne, Lavendar met Stephen's son, Paul Irving, with whom she instantly formed a deep, maternal bond. Upon learning of her whereabouts from Paul, Stephen Irving returned to Prince Edward Island to seek out Lavendar. The two reconciled, rekindling their old affection, and were married in the garden at Echo Lodge in the late summer. Following their wedding, they embarked on a trip to the Pacific coast and subsequently settled in Boston, returning to spend their summers at Echo Lodge.

label: History
value: Kenneth was killed in a wagon accident.
unit: Leslie's early life in Four Winds was marked by tragedy: her beloved brother Kenneth was killed in a wagon accident, and two years later her despondent father hanged himself. To save her widowed mother from being evicted from their farm, sixteen-year-old Leslie agreed to marry Dick Moore, whom she did not love. Shortly after her mother's death, Dick sailed away on the Four Sisters and disappeared. Captain Jim later found an amnesiac man in Havana whom he believed to be Dick Moore and brought him back to Four Winds. For twelve years, Leslie faithfully cared for the brain-damaged man, living in poverty and isolation in her ancestral homestead. Upon the arrival of Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe at Four Winds, Leslie initially felt a bitter envy toward Anne's happiness. However, she eventually confessed her feelings to Anne, breaking down her emotional barriers, and the two became devoted friends. When Gilbert suggested an operation that might restore Dick's memory, Leslie courageously agreed despite her dread of returning to a life with the man she had once loathed. The operation in Montreal succeeded in restoring the man's memory, revealing that he was actually Dick's cousin, George Moore, and that the real Dick Moore had died years earlier in Cuba. Finally freed from her tragic burden, Leslie returned to Four Winds. She fell in love with Owen Ford, a writer who had stayed at her house during the summer while writing his novel based on Captain Jim's life-book. They confessed their mutual love in Anne's garden, and Owen proposed to her.

label: History
value: Marilla Cuthbert lived at Green Gables.
unit: Marilla Cuthbert lived at Green Gables with her brother Matthew, managing the household while he farmed the land. Deciding to adopt an orphan boy to help on the farm, they were mistakenly sent an eleven-year-old girl, Anne Shirley. Although Marilla initially intended to send Anne back, she agreed to keep her at Matthew's insistence and took charge of her upbringing. Over the years, Marilla grew deeply attached to Anne, guiding her into young womanhood and supporting her education at Queen's Academy and later Redmond College. Following Matthew's sudden death, Marilla faced the prospect of selling Green Gables due to failing eyesight, but Anne chose to stay home to teach and care for her. Later, Marilla agreed to take in her orphaned third cousins once removed, the twins Davy and Dora Keith. To enable Anne to attend college, Marilla invited her lifelong friend, Rachel Lynde, to move into Green Gables to live with her. In her later years, Marilla remained at Green Gables, welcoming Anne back for her marriage to Gilbert Blythe, and watching over her grandchildren and the community.

Although Marilla initially intended to send Anne back, she agreed to keep her at Matthew's insistence and took charge of her upbringing. Over the years, Marilla grew deeply attached to Anne, guiding her into young womanhood and supporting her education at Queen's Academy and later Redmond College. Following Matthew's sudden death, Marilla faced the prospect of selling Green Gables due to failing eyesight, but Anne chose to stay home to teach and care for her. Later, Marilla agreed to take in her orphaned third cousins once removed, the twins Davy and Dora Keith. To enable Anne to attend college, Marilla invited her lifelong friend, Rachel Lynde, to move into Green Gables to live with her. In her later years, Marilla remained at Green Gables, welcoming Anne back for her marriage to Gilbert Blythe, and watching over her grandchildren and the community.

label: Appearance
value: Marshall Elliott is a tall man.
unit: Marshall Elliott is a tall, broad-shouldered man with a strong, clean-shaven chin and frank gray eyes. For fifteen years, due to a political vow, he wore a river of crinkly brown beard reaching nearly to his knees and a corresponding cascade of thick, wavy brown hair down his back, giving him the look of a dime museum freak or a Viking. After shaving his beard and cutting his hair, he was revealed as a handsome, well-featured man with a mane of red hair.

value: Marshall Elliott is a passionate man.

He possesses a strong sense of honor, refusing to break his word once given. He is also capable of great generosity and kindness, being deeply moved to anger by any mistreatment of children.

label: History
value: Mary Vance ran away from her abusive guardian
unit: Mary Vance ran away from her abusive guardian, Mrs. Wiley, after learning she was to be sent to an even harsher relative. Losing her saved money on her way to Glen St. Mary, she hid in an old barn in Mr. Taylor's pasture for two days without food until the Meredith children found her and brought her to the manse. She stayed at the manse for two weeks, helping with housework while defying Aunt Martha, and became a regular playmate of the Meredith and Blythe children in Rainbow Valley. Following the sudden death of Mrs. Wiley, Una Meredith pleaded with Miss Cornelia (Mrs. Marshall Elliott) to adopt Mary. Miss Cornelia consented, taking Mary into her home, where Mary blossomed under good food, new clothes, and strict discipline, proving herself to be an energetic worker. She continued joining the children's gatherings in Rainbow Valley and eventually settled contentedly into her new life.

label: History
value: Matthew Cuthbert lives at Green Gables
unit: Matthew Cuthbert lives at Green Gables with his sister Marilla. Due to his failing health and advancing age, he and Marilla decide to adopt an orphan boy from Nova Scotia to help on the farm. Upon going to the Bright River station to fetch the boy, he finds eleven-year-old Anne Shirley instead and brings her home, unable to break the news of the mistake to her himself. Captivated by her chatter, Matthew quietly insists to Marilla that they keep the orphan girl. Throughout Anne's upbringing, Matthew acts as her constant champion and confidant, secretly indulging her wishes, such as buying her a fashionable dress with puffed sleeves for Christmas. When Anne passes her college entrance exams and later wins the Avery Scholarship, Matthew expresses immense pride in her achievements. Shortly after Anne completes her studies at Queen's Academy, the Abbey Bank fails, wiping out the Cuthbert family savings; the shock causes Matthew to collapse and die instantly of heart failure. He is buried in the Avonlea graveyard.

value: During a fiercely contested general election fifteen years prior, Norman Douglas made a vow at a public meeting.
unit: During a fiercely contested general election fifteen years prior, Norman Douglas made a vow at a public meeting that he would neither shave his face nor cut his hair until the Liberal party (Grits) returned to power. As the Conservatives remained in office, he maintained his vow for a decade and a half, growing a long, flowing beard and mane of hair that made him famous across Four Winds. When the Liberals finally won a general election years later, he immediately went to the local barber in the middle of the night, forced him to shave his beard and trim his hair, and abandoned his wild appearance. Soon afterward, he began attending church again, renewing his acquaintance with his old flame, Ellen West, whom he had courted thirty years earlier before marrying his late wife Hester. Despite an initial impasse caused by a vow Ellen and her sister Rosemary had made, Faith Meredith intervened to resolve their misunderstandings, leading Norman to propose directly. Ellen accepted his proposal, and the two were married in a double wedding alongside Reverend John Meredith and Rosemary West, after which Norman moved to Ellen's farm on the hill.

As the Conservatives remained in office, he maintained his vow for a decade and a half, growing a long, flowing beard and mane of hair that made him famous across Four Winds. When the Liberals finally won a general election years later, he immediately went to the local barber in the middle of the night, forced him to shave his beard and trim his hair, and abandoned his wild appearance. Soon afterward, he began attending church again, renewing his acquaintance with his old flame, Ellen West, whom he had courted thirty years earlier before marrying his late wife Hester. Despite an initial impasse caused by a vow Ellen and her sister Rosemary had made, Faith Meredith intervened to resolve their misunderstandings, leading Norman to propose directly. Ellen accepted his proposal, and the two were married in a double wedding alongside Reverend John Meredith and Rosemary West, after which Norman moved to Ellen's farm on the hill.

label: History
value: Owen Ford came to Four Winds
unit: Owen Ford came to Four Winds to recuperate after a severe attack of typhoid fever, boarding at the house of Leslie Moore. Upon his arrival, he met Anne and Gilbert Blythe, who introduced him to Captain Jim Boyd at the Four Winds Light. Discovering Captain Jim's logbook of sea-faring adventures, Owen recognized its immense narrative value and decided to collaborate with the old captain to write a novel based on his life. Throughout the summer, he worked on the manuscript at the lighthouse, forming a deep friendship with Captain Jim, Anne, and Leslie. During this time, he fell intensely in love with Leslie, but kept his feelings concealed when he believed she was bound irrevocably to her incapacitated husband, Dick Moore. After completing his novel, Owen confessed his love to Anne before departing Four Winds, believing he would never see Leslie again. Later, when it was revealed through a surgical operation that Leslie's husband was actually his deceased cousin George, Leslie became a free woman. Upon learning of her freedom, Owen returned to Four Winds, declared his love to Leslie in Anne's garden, and became engaged to her. He eventually purchased the little house of dreams to serve as their summer home, and his book, The Life-Book of Captain Jim, was published to great critical and commercial acclaim.

unit: Owen Ford came to Four Winds to recuperate after a severe attack of typhoid fever, boarding at the house of Leslie Moore. Upon his arrival, he met Anne and Gilbert Blythe, who introduced him to Captain Jim Boyd at the Four Winds Light. Discovering Captain Jim's logbook of sea-faring adventures, Owen recognized its immense narrative value and decided to collaborate with the old captain to write a novel based on his life. Throughout the summer, he worked on the manuscript at the lighthouse, forming a deep friendship with Captain Jim, Anne, and Leslie. During this time, he fell intensely in love with Leslie, but kept his feelings concealed when he believed she was bound irrevocably to her incapacitated husband, Dick Moore. After completing his novel, Owen confessed his love to Anne before departing Four Winds, believing he would never see Leslie again. Later, when it was revealed through a surgical operation that Leslie's husband was actually his deceased cousin George, Leslie became a free woman. Upon learning of her freedom, Owen returned to Four Winds, declared his love to Leslie in Anne's garden, and became engaged to her. He eventually purchased the little house of dreams to serve as their summer home, and his book, The Life-Book of Captain Jim, was published to great critical and commercial acclaim.

label: History
value: Paul Irving arrives in Avonlea to live with his grandmother.
unit: Paul Irving arrives in Avonlea to live with his grandmother and attends Avonlea school, quickly bonding with his new teacher, Anne Shirley, over their shared imaginative nature. He shares his inner world of 'rock people' with Anne, who becomes his mentor and closest friend. He later introduces Anne to Miss Lavendar Lewis at Echo Lodge, unwittingly helping to set in motion the reunion and marriage of Miss Lavendar and his father, Stephen Irving. Following his father's remarriage, Paul happily accepts Miss Lavendar as his 'Mother Lavendar' and spends his summers with them at Echo Lodge. As he grows older, Paul begins writing poetry, developing his literary talent. After completing his schooling at Avonlea, he goes abroad for two years of study.

label: History
value: Philippa Gordon arrived at Redmond College in Kingsport.
unit: Philippa Gordon arrived at Redmond College in Kingsport, initially feeling lonesome until she encountered Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant in Old St. John's Cemetery. She quickly struck up an affectionate friendship with them and brought them into her wide social circle. During her first year, she struggled to choose between her two home suitors, Alec and Alonzo, while enjoying the devotion of numerous campus admirers. Prior to their second year at Redmond, she joined Anne, Priscilla, and Stella Maynard in renting Patty's Place on Spofford Avenue, where they lived with Aunt Jamesina. Over a summer at Prospect Point, she met Jonas Blake, an earnest and homely theology student; despite her previous declarations that she must marry a rich and handsome man, she fell deeply in love with him. After finally declining her former suitors, she happily accepted Jonas's proposal during her Junior year. Upon completing her Arts course at Redmond, Philippa married Jonas in a June wedding and moved to his mission parish in the Patterson Street slums.

label: History
value: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster for the Avonlea school.
unit: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster for the Avonlea school. During his tenure, he spent much of his time at the back of the classroom explaining lessons to Prissy Andrews, with whom he was courting, while neglecting his younger pupils and allowing the rest of the school to do as they pleased. He was known for his sarcastic punishments, such as forcing Anne Shirley to stand in front of the blackboard with a humiliating inscription after she broke her slate over Gilbert Blythe's head, or making her sit with Gilbert for being late. He also whipped Sam Boulter for talking back in class. After completing his term, he delivered a tearful farewell speech to his students upon his departure from the school.

He was known for his sarcastic punishments, such as forcing Anne Shirley to stand in front of the blackboard with a humiliating inscription after she broke her slate over Gilbert Blythe's head, or making her sit with Gilbert for being late. He also whipped Sam Boulter for talking back in class. After completing his term, he delivered a tearful farewell speech to his students upon his departure from the school.

label: History
value: Priscilla Grant attended Queen's Academy
unit: Priscilla Grant attended Queen's Academy with Anne Shirley and later taught at the school in Carmody. Desiring to further her education, she resigned from her teaching position and enrolled at Redmond College in Kingsport alongside Anne. Together with Anne, Philippa Gordon, and Stella Maynard, she lived at Patty's Place under the care of Aunt Jamesina, enjoying a rich social and academic life. During her college years, she specialized in Classics, eventually earning High Honors upon graduation. After completing her studies at Redmond, Priscilla travelled to Japan to work or teach, continuing her life's adventures abroad.

value: Jonas Blake attended Redmond College
unit: Jonas Blake attended Redmond College and St. Columbia to prepare for the ministry. While serving a summer mission at Prospect Point, he met Philippa Gordon, who nicknamed him 'Jonas' and 'Jo.' He married Philippa Gordon in June following their graduation, and later attended the wedding of Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe at Green Gables, where he delivered the nuptial prayer.

label: History
value: Rilla Blythe grew up.
unit: Rilla Blythe grew up as the youngest child of the Blythe family at Ingleside. On one occasion, she was entrusted by Susan Baker to deliver a basket of early strawberries to Mr. Meredith or Aunt Martha at the manse. Dressed in her best clothes, she strutted through the village street, where she encountered Mary Vance. Mary attempted to take the basket from her, but Rilla firmly refused to surrender it. In retaliation, Mary threatened her with a large dried codfish, causing Rilla to flee in terror. During the chase, Rilla tripped and fell into a mud-puddle at the end of the street, ruining her fine clothes and hat, before being rescued by Miss Cornelia.

label: History
value: Rosemary West grew up in the Glen St. Mary area.
unit: Rosemary West grew up in the Glen St. Mary area. At seventeen, her first love, Martin Crawford, was lost at sea, leaving her heartbroken. Following her mother's death years later, she made a solemn vow on her mother's Bible to her sister Ellen that she would never marry, so that Ellen would not be left alone. She lived quietly at the family homestead on a hill, giving music lessons to local children. Eventually, she met the widowed minister, John Meredith, and the two developed a deep mutual affection. When John proposed, Rosemary felt bound by her oath to Ellen and reluctantly refused him. Later, after Ellen decided to marry her own former suitor, Norman Douglas, and released Rosemary from her vow, John Meredith was encouraged by his young daughter Una to ask again. Rosemary accepted, and they were married in a double wedding alongside Ellen and Norman.

label: History
value: Roy Gardner originally attended Redmond College for his Freshman and Sophomore years.
unit: Roy Gardner originally attended Redmond College for his Freshman and Sophomore years, but paused his studies to accompany his mother to Europe for two years due to her failing health. Upon returning to Redmond as a Junior, he rescued Anne Shirley in the rain under a collapsed umbrella, marking the beginning of their courtship. He wooed Anne attentively over two years with flowers, compliments, and poetry, earning the acceptance of her friends and eventually his own family. After their graduation, Roy proposed to Anne in the harbor pavilion at Kingsport where they first met, but she unexpectedly rejected his proposal upon realizing she did not truly love him. Though deeply hurt and believing his life ruined at the time, Roy eventually recovered from the heartbreak and later married another woman.

label: Personality
value: Ruby was cheerful.
unit: Ruby was cheerful, good-tempered, and loved the pleasant things of life, though she was undeniably shallow, vain, and sentimental. She had an hysterical streak and was prone to fits of tears or laughter. Obsessed with boys, courtships, and beaux from a young age, she measured her success by her romantic conquests. She fought hard against accepting her fatal illness, maintaining a cheerful facade until she finally faced her fear of death in a tender confession to Anne.

label: History
value: Ruby Gillis grew up in Avonlea
unit: Ruby Gillis grew up in Avonlea as a schoolmate of Anne Shirley and Diana Barry. During their schooldays, she was known for her beauty, her numerous beaux, and her tendency to turn hysterical in emergencies. She joined the girls' Story Club, contributing overly sentimental tales. After studying for the Entrance at Avonlea School, she attended Queen's Academy alongside Anne and earned a teacher's license. She taught for a time in Carmody, where she continued her active romantic pursuits, but contracted a severe lung congestion during the winter. This developed into galloping consumption, forcing her to quit teaching. Throughout her illness, Ruby maintained a cheerful front and insisted she would recover to teach at White Sands. Shortly before her death, she broke down to Anne Shirley, confessing her terror of dying and her grief at leaving the world behind. She passed away calmly in her sleep that autumn and was buried in the Avonlea graveyard.

label: History
value: Miss Muriel Stacy was hired by the school trustees.
unit: Miss Muriel Stacy was hired by the school trustees as the first female teacher in Avonlea. She quickly gained the devotion of her pupils, including Anne Shirley, through her sympathetic nature and innovative teaching methods, such as nature study field trips and physical culture exercises. When the scholars wished to raise money for a school flag, Miss Stacy organized a Christmas Night concert in the hall. After her first year, she declined a position in her home district to remain at Avonlea and guide her advanced students through the Entrance examinations for Queen's Academy, offering them extra lessons after school. Following the successful completion of the term and the passing of her Queen's Class pupils, Miss Stacy left Avonlea. She eventually married and moved to California.

label: History
value: Stella Maynard attended Queen's Academy
unit: Stella Maynard attended Queen's Academy alongside Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant, where she became part of their close-knit circle of friends. After graduation, she taught at a country school for two years, experiencing all the trials and humorous tribulations of a young teacher. Weary of boarding and country schoolteaching, she decided to resume her studies at Redmond College to complete her Arts degree. She proposed that she, Anne, Priscilla, and Philippa Gordon rent a house together in Kingsport, bringing her Aunt Jamesina to keep house for them. The girls established themselves at Patty's Place, where Stella shared a room with Priscilla. At Redmond, Stella maintained a good all-round academic standing and graduated with her B.A. degree. After graduation, she accepted a position teaching in Vancouver.

label: History
value: Susan Baker was engaged as the maid-of-all-work.
unit: Susan Baker was engaged as the maid-of-all-work and housekeeper for Dr. Gilbert Blythe and Anne Shirley at their first home in Four Winds. She took complete charge of the domestic management of the household, priding herself on her culinary accomplishments and dedicated service. When Anne gave birth to her son Shirley after a life-threatening illness, Susan nursed the infant constantly and claimed him as her special nursling. She later moved with the family to their new home at Ingleside in Glen St. Mary. During the Blythes' three-month trip to Europe, Susan cared for Shirley at her brother's home while the other children visited Avonlea. Upon their return, she resumed her position as the indispensable pillar of the Ingleside household.

value: Una Meredith moved from Maywater to the Glen St.

She befriended Mary Vance, a homeless runaway whom the Meredith children found hiding in an old barn, and took her into the manse. Troubled by local gossip regarding her family's unruly behavior, Una joined her siblings in forming a 'Good-Conduct Club' to discipline themselves. Fearing that gossip about her family was preventing her father from marrying Rosemary West, and terrified by stories of cruel stepmothers, Una secretly visited Rosemary West to ask her to marry her father, promising that the children would be good. Upon learning the truth, Rosemary entrusted Una with a message that led to her father's successful proposal. Following her father's engagement, Una looked forward eagerly to learning household skills and welcoming Rosemary into their family.

Troubled by local gossip regarding her family's unruly behavior, Una joined her siblings in forming a 'Good-Conduct Club' to discipline themselves. During a self-imposed fast for the club, she fainted from hunger during a Sunday evening church service, causing a local sensation. Fearing that gossip about her family was preventing her father from marrying Rosemary West, and terrified by stories of cruel stepmothers, Una secretly visited Rosemary West to ask her to marry her father, promising that the children would be good. Upon learning the truth, Rosemary entrusted Una with a message that led to her father's successful proposal. Following her father's engagement, Una looked forward eagerly to learning household skills and welcoming Rosemary into their family.

label: History
value: Walter grew up at Ingleside
unit: Walter grew up at Ingleside in Glen St. Mary as the second child of Gilbert and Anne Blythe. He spent much of his childhood playing with his siblings and the Meredith children in their favorite haunt, Rainbow Valley, where he frequently read poetry and myths to the group. Though regarded as somewhat delicate and quiet by his peers, he developed a deep friendship with the minister, Mr. Meredith, and his sister Di. During one school year, after enduring severe toothaches and facing insults directed at his mother and Faith Meredith by Dan Reese, Walter confronted Dan and defeated him in a fistfight, earning respect for his bravery. Later, he suffered a severe bout of toothache which he courageously resolved to face by visiting the dentist. As he grew older, he continued to cultivate his poetic talents, often envisioning a future filled with travel and adventure, while sharing a mysterious premonition of a Pied Piper drawing him and his friends away from Rainbow Valley.
